title: Ezekiel Chapter 13 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 13 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 13 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 13.

questions.question: Who is Ezekiel instructed to prophesy against in Ezekiel 13?
options: The prophets of Israel that prophesy out of their own hearts
The kings of Israel
The priests of Israel
The elders of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The prophets of Israel that prophesy out of their own hearts
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:2 instructs Ezekiel to prophesy against the prophets of Israel who prophesy out of their own hearts.

questions.question: What does the Lord say about the prophets who follow their own spirit and have seen nothing?
options: Woe unto them, for they are foolish
They shall be rewarded
They shall be given visions
They shall be made leaders
questions.correctAnswer: Woe unto them, for they are foolish
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:3 states, 'Woe unto the foolish prophets, that follow their own spirit, and have seen nothing!'

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 13, to what are the prophets of Israel compared?
options: Foxes in the deserts
Lions in the forest
Eagles in the sky
Sheep in the field
questions.correctAnswer: Foxes in the deserts
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:4 says, 'O Israel, thy prophets are like the foxes in the deserts.'

questions.question: What have the prophets of Israel failed to do according to Ezekiel 13:5?
options: They have not gone up into the gaps, nor made up the hedge for the house of Israel
They have not prayed for the people
They have not written the law
They have not built altars
questions.correctAnswer: They have not gone up into the gaps, nor made up the hedge for the house of Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:5 clearly states that the prophets 'have not gone up into the gaps, neither made up the hedge for the house of Israel.'

questions.question: What kind of divination have the prophets seen and spoken, according to Ezekiel 13?
options: Vanity and lying divination
True and holy divination
Dreams and visions
Prophecies of hope
questions.correctAnswer: Vanity and lying divination
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:6 says, 'They have seen vanity and lying divination, saying, The LORD saith: and the LORD hath not sent them.'

questions.question: True or False: The prophets said 'The LORD saith it' even though the LORD had not spoken.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:7 explains that the prophets spoke lying divination saying 'The LORD saith it;' albeit the LORD had not spoken.

questions.question: What is the Lord's response to the prophets who have spoken vanity and seen lies?
options: He is against them
He will bless them
He will ignore them
He will reward them
questions.correctAnswer: He is against them
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:8 states, 'Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Because ye have spoken vanity, and seen lies, therefore, behold, I am against you.'

questions.question: True or False: The hand of the Lord shall be upon the prophets that see vanity and divine lies.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:9 says, 'And mine hand shall be upon the prophets that see vanity, and that divine lies.'

questions.question: What false message did the prophets seduce the people with?
options: Peace, when there was no peace
War, when there was peace
Prosperity, when there was famine
Safety, when there was danger
questions.correctAnswer: Peace, when there was no peace
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:10 states, 'Because, even because they have seduced my people, saying, Peace; and there was no peace.'

questions.question: True or False: The prophets built a strong and lasting wall for the house of Israel.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:10-11 describes how one built a wall and others daubed it with untempered mortar, which will fall and be destroyed.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 13, what will happen to the wall that was daubed with untempered mortar?
options: It shall fall and be destroyed by overflowing showers and hailstones
It shall stand strong forever
It shall be rebuilt by the people
It shall be blessed by the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: It shall fall and be destroyed by overflowing showers and hailstones
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:11 says, 'Say unto them which daub it with untempered morter, that it shall fall: there shall be an overflowing shower; and ye, O great hailstones, shall fall.'

questions.question: What will be revealed when the wall falls, according to Ezekiel 13?
options: The foundation thereof shall be discovered
The treasures hidden behind the wall
The names of the builders
The location of the enemies
questions.correctAnswer: The foundation thereof shall be discovered
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:14 states, '...so that the foundation thereof shall be discovered, and it shall fall.'

questions.question: In Ezekiel 13, what is the Lord's attitude toward the women who prophesy out of their own heart?
options: Woe unto them for sewing pillows and hunting souls
Praise for their faithfulness
Indifference toward their actions
Reward for their visions
questions.correctAnswer: Woe unto them for sewing pillows and hunting souls
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:18 pronounces woe upon the women who 'sew pillows to all armholes, and make kerchiefs upon the head of every stature to hunt souls.'

questions.question: Which comes first in Ezekiel 13: the Lord declaring woe upon the foolish prophets or the comparison of the prophets to foxes?
options: The Lord declaring woe upon the foolish prophets
The comparison of the prophets to foxes
Both occur simultaneously
Neither occurs in chapter 13
questions.correctAnswer: The Lord declaring woe upon the foolish prophets
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:3 mentions the woe upon foolish prophets before Ezekiel 13:4 compares them to foxes.

questions.question: True or False: The Lord promises to deliver His people from the hand of the lying women prophets.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:23 states, 'I will deliver my people out of your hand,' referring to the lying women prophets.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 13 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 13 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 13:9, what consequence will the prophets who divine lies and see vanity face?
options: They shall not be in the assembly of God's people
They shall be promoted among the people
They shall receive a crown of righteousness
They shall become leaders in the land
questions.correctAnswer: They shall not be in the assembly of God's people
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:9 states that the hand of the Lord shall be upon the false prophets who see vanity and divine lies, and they shall not be in the assembly of His people, nor be written in the book of Israel, nor enter the land of Israel. This shows the severe exclusion as a consequence for their falsehood.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 13:10 describe as the cause of the false sense of security among the people?
options: Prophets seducing the people by saying 'Peace' when there is no peace
The people's refusal to listen to God's word
Enemies building walls around Israel
The destruction of the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Prophets seducing the people by saying 'Peace' when there is no peace
questions.explanation: Verse 10 explains that false prophets seduced the people by proclaiming peace when there was none, and they built a wall that others daubed with untempered mortar, symbolizing a faulty and insecure protection.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'untempered morter' mentioned in Ezekiel 13:11-14?
options: It represents false security that will fail under judgment
It symbolizes a strong and lasting foundation
It is a metaphor for God’s mercy
It indicates the building of a new temple
questions.correctAnswer: It represents false security that will fail under judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 11-14 describe how the wall daubed with untempered morter will fall under stormy wind and hailstones, revealing the foundation and causing destruction. This symbolizes the false security given by the lying prophets that will be destroyed by God's judgment.

questions.question: Based on Ezekiel 13:15-16, what will happen to the prophets who prophesy peace for Jerusalem when there is no peace?
options: They will be exposed and the wall they built will be no more
They will be rewarded for their encouragement
They will lead the people into battle
They will be forgiven and restored
questions.correctAnswer: They will be exposed and the wall they built will be no more
questions.explanation: These verses explain that God's wrath will be accomplished on the wall and those who daubed it with untempered morter, meaning the false prophets who proclaim false peace will be exposed and their protection will vanish.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 13:17-18 warn against certain women among the prophets?
options: They sew pillows to armholes and make kerchiefs to hunt souls
They lead the people in prayer and worship
They build strong walls for protection
They teach the law faithfully
questions.correctAnswer: They sew pillows to armholes and make kerchiefs to hunt souls
questions.explanation: Verse 18 describes women prophets who use symbolic actions like sewing pillows to armholes and kerchiefs on heads to hunt souls, indicating deceptive practices that harm God's people.

questions.question: What is God's response to the women who hunt souls for a price, according to Ezekiel 13:19-20?
options: God will tear their pillows and let the souls go free
God will reward them for their work
God will bless their ministry
God will multiply their wealth
questions.correctAnswer: God will tear their pillows and let the souls go free
questions.explanation: Verses 19-20 explain that God is against the women who pollute Him by hunting souls for barley and bread; He will tear their pillows (instruments of deception) and release the souls they hunted to make fly.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 13:21-22, what effect have the lying prophets had on the righteous and the wicked?
options: They have made the righteous sad and strengthened the wicked
They have comforted the righteous and punished the wicked
They have led both to repentance
They have brought peace to all
questions.correctAnswer: They have made the righteous sad and strengthened the wicked
questions.explanation: Verses 21-22 show that the lies of the prophets caused sadness in the righteous, whom God did not intend to be sad, and encouraged the wicked not to repent by promising them life falsely.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 13:23 promise will happen as a result of God's intervention against false prophets?
options: There will be no more vanity or lying divinations
False prophets will multiply
The people will remain deceived
The lying prophets will become rulers
questions.correctAnswer: There will be no more vanity or lying divinations
questions.explanation: Verse 23 states that God will deliver His people out of the hand of false prophets so that no more vanity or lying divinations will occur, affirming His protection and justice.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 13:12 suggests that when the false wall falls, people will question the quality of the daubing used.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:12 says that when the wall has fallen, it will be asked where the daubing with untempered mortar is, indicating the failure and exposure of the faulty work.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 13:4 compares the prophets of Israel to lions in the deserts.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:4 compares the prophets of Israel to foxes in the deserts, not lions, indicating their cunning but destructive nature.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ezekiel 13:2-3, some prophets prophesy from their own hearts and have seen nothing from God.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verses 2-3 warn against prophets who prophesy from their own spirit and have seen nothing, highlighting their foolishness and falsehood.

questions.question: What practical lesson about integrity can we learn from Ezekiel 13:6-7 regarding false prophecy?
options: One should not claim to speak for God without His sending
It is acceptable to speak comforting words even if untrue
Deceiving others is justified for peace
Prophets should rely on their own visions
questions.correctAnswer: One should not claim to speak for God without His sending
questions.explanation: Verses 6-7 condemn those who say 'The LORD saith' when He has not sent them, teaching that claiming divine authority falsely is wrong and damages trust and integrity.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 13:10-11 illustrate the consequences of false assurances given by leaders?
options: False assurances lead to collapse and destruction like a wall falling under hail and storm
False assurances bring lasting peace and protection
False assurances build strong, unbreakable walls
False assurances encourage genuine repentance
questions.correctAnswer: False assurances lead to collapse and destruction like a wall falling under hail and storm
questions.explanation: Verses 10-11 use the metaphor of a wall built and daubed with untempered mortar that will fall under stormy wind and hailstones, showing that false assurances lead to ruin.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 13:16, what is the nature of the visions the false prophets see about Jerusalem?
options: Visions of peace when there is no peace
Visions of destruction and judgment
Visions of exile and mourning
Visions of God's wrath
questions.correctAnswer: Visions of peace when there is no peace
questions.explanation: Verse 16 criticizes the prophets of Israel who prophesy concerning Jerusalem and see visions of peace when in reality there is no peace, illustrating their deceit.

questions.question: What practical Christian virtue does Ezekiel 13:22 teach by condemning the prophets who strengthen the wicked by promising life?
options: Integrity and honest accountability
Generosity in giving
Humility in leadership
Forgiveness towards enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Integrity and honest accountability
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:22 shows that lying to strengthen the wicked and promise life falsely is condemned, teaching the importance of integrity and accountability in speaking truth.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 13 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 13.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 13:18, what items do the women sew and make to hunt souls?
options: Pillows to all armholes and kerchiefs upon the head
Ropes and nets
Garments of sorrow and chains
Crowns and scepters
questions.correctAnswer: Pillows to all armholes and kerchiefs upon the head
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:18 specifically states that the women sew pillows to all armholes and make kerchiefs upon the head to hunt souls, symbolizing deceptive practices used to ensnare God's people.

questions.question: What consequence does God declare against the pillows used for hunting souls in Ezekiel 13:20?
options: He will tear them from their arms and let the souls go
He will bless them for their efforts
He will multiply their effectiveness
He will hide them in the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: He will tear them from their arms and let the souls go
questions.explanation: Verse 20 declares God's judgment against the pillows used to 'hunt souls', stating He will tear them from the women's arms and release the souls they captured.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 13:21 say will happen to the kerchiefs and the people held by the women who prophesy falsely?
options: The kerchiefs will be torn, and God will deliver His people
The kerchiefs will be strengthened, and people will be trapped forever
The kerchiefs will multiply, and new souls will be hunted
The kerchiefs will be hidden, and the people will remain captive
questions.correctAnswer: The kerchiefs will be torn, and God will deliver His people
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:21 announces that God will tear the kerchiefs and deliver His people from the hands of these false prophets, ending their captivity.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 13:22, what effect do lies have on the righteous and the wicked?
options: Make the righteous sad and strengthen the wicked
Make the righteous joyful and the wicked repentant
Have no effect on either
Make the wicked sad and strengthen the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: Make the righteous sad and strengthen the wicked
questions.explanation: Verse 22 describes how lies sadden the righteous—though God did not intend this—and embolden the wicked by promising them life, preventing their repentance.

questions.question: What final assurance does God give in Ezekiel 13:23 regarding the fate of His people and the false prophets?
options: God will deliver His people and the false prophets will see no more vanity
God will abandon His people to the false prophets
The false prophets will be exalted, and the people subdued
God will remain silent forever
questions.correctAnswer: God will deliver His people and the false prophets will see no more vanity
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:23 promises that God will deliver His people from the false prophets, who will no longer see vanity or divine divinations, affirming His sovereignty.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word translated as 'kerchiefs' in Ezekiel 13:18, and what does it symbolize in this context?
options: A head covering symbolizing deceitful control over souls
A garment of mourning symbolizing sorrow
A crown symbolizing false authority
A sash symbolizing purity
questions.correctAnswer: A head covering symbolizing deceitful control over souls
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term for 'kerchiefs' (מִטְפָּחוֹת, mitpachot) refers to head coverings. In Ezekiel 13:18, they symbolize deceptive practices used by false prophetesses to entrap and control the souls of God's people.

questions.question: Ezekiel 13:17 commands the prophet to set his face against which group?
options: The daughters of the people who prophesy out of their own heart
The elders of Israel
The priests in the temple
The foreign nations
questions.correctAnswer: The daughters of the people who prophesy out of their own heart
questions.explanation: Verse 17 instructs Ezekiel to confront the women of Israel who prophesy from their own hearts rather than by God's word, highlighting their culpability.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 13:16 describe the false prophets' messages about Jerusalem?
options: They prophesy peace when there is no peace
They warn of destruction only
They call for rebellion against Babylon
They speak only of exile
questions.correctAnswer: They prophesy peace when there is no peace
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:16 condemns prophets who falsely promise peace for Jerusalem despite the reality of impending judgment, misleading the people.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Ezekiel 13:10-15 to describe the false security given by the prophets?
options: Metaphor of a wall daubed with untempered mortar
Simile comparing prophets to sheep
Chiasmus about peace and war
Parable of the sower
questions.correctAnswer: Metaphor of a wall daubed with untempered mortar
questions.explanation: Verses 10-15 use the metaphor of a wall patched with untempered mortar to illustrate the fragile and false security the prophets give, which will ultimately collapse.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 13:9 declares that prophets who divine lies will be included in the assembly of God's people.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:9 explicitly states that prophets who see vanity and divine lies will not be in the assembly of God's people, nor written in the book of Israel, nor enter the land, confirming exclusion.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 13:6 reveal about the nature of the prophecies given by the false prophets?
options: They are vanity and lying divinations falsely claiming the LORD's word
They are true and faithful messages from God
They are silent and secretive
They are only warnings of destruction
questions.correctAnswer: They are vanity and lying divinations falsely claiming the LORD's word
questions.explanation: Verse 6 condemns false prophets who speak vanity and lies, claiming 'The LORD saith,' though God did not send them, deceiving the people.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage shares a similar condemnation of false prophecy as Ezekiel 13?
options: Jeremiah 23:16-22
Genesis 1:1-5
Psalm 23
Matthew 5:1-12
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah 23:16-22
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 23:16-22 also condemns false prophets who deceive Israel with lies, paralleling Ezekiel 13's themes of false prophecy and God's judgment.

questions.question: What historical context helps explain the criticism of prophets in Ezekiel 13?
options: The impending Babylonian exile and false hopes for peace
The Exodus from Egypt
The conquest of Canaan
The reign of King David
questions.correctAnswer: The impending Babylonian exile and false hopes for peace
questions.explanation: Ezekiel prophesied during the Babylonian exile period, where false prophets falsely assured peace despite looming judgment, which is the context for his harsh rebuke.

questions.question: Ezekiel 13:4 compares the prophets of Israel to what animal, highlighting their character?
options: Foxes in the deserts
Lions in the forest
Doves in the sky
Serpents in the grass
questions.correctAnswer: Foxes in the deserts
questions.explanation: Verse 4 likens Israel's prophets to foxes in the deserts, symbolizing their cunning and destructiveness rather than protective strength.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ezekiel 13:19, the false prophetesses polluted God among His people for material gain.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:19 states that the women polluted God among His people for handfuls of barley and pieces of bread, indicating they accepted bribes to lie and deceive.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 13 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 13 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What sin are the prophets of Israel accused of in Ezekiel 13:3?
options: Prophesying out of their own spirit without seeing anything
Leading people to worship idols
Ignoring the poor and needy
Refusing to enter the promised land
questions.correctAnswer: Prophesying out of their own spirit without seeing anything
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:3 condemns the foolish prophets who follow their own spirit and have seen nothing, indicating they falsely claim divine revelation.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 13:5, what failure is attributed to the prophets concerning Israel's protection?
options: They have not gone up into the gaps or made up the hedge to protect Israel
They built idolatrous altars
They refused to warn Israel of impending judgment
They neglected to teach the law of Moses
questions.correctAnswer: They have not gone up into the gaps or made up the hedge to protect Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 5 explains the prophets did not repair the breaches ('gaps') or build protective barriers ('hedge') for Israel, symbolizing their neglect in spiritual defense.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 13:6 say about the nature of the divinations made by the prophets?
options: They are vanity and lying divinations falsely claiming the LORD's word
They are faithful and true messages from God
They are warnings of coming exile
They are calls for repentance
questions.correctAnswer: They are vanity and lying divinations falsely claiming the LORD's word
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:6 states that the prophets' divinations are vain and false, and they wrongly say 'The LORD saith' when God has not sent them.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in God's judgment against false prophets in Ezekiel 13:8?
options: God's justice in opposing vanity and lies
God's mercy towards sinners
God's omnipresence among His people
God's grace in forgiving repentant prophets
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice in opposing vanity and lies
questions.explanation: Verse 8 shows God's justice as He declares opposition against those who speak vanity and see lies, emphasizing His holiness and righteousness.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 13:9, what is the consequence for prophets who divine lies and see vanity?
options: They will not be in the assembly of God's people nor enter the land of Israel
They will be rewarded with prophecy gifts
They will be given a second chance to repent
They will become leaders in Israel
questions.correctAnswer: They will not be in the assembly of God's people nor enter the land of Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 9 states God’s hand will be upon these false prophets, barring them from the assembly and the land, signifying judgment and exclusion.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 13:10-11 describe the false security the prophets give to the people?
options: They promise peace and build walls patched with untempered mortar, which will fall
They preach repentance and restoration
They warn of exile and destruction
They call for fasting and prayer
questions.correctAnswer: They promise peace and build walls patched with untempered mortar, which will fall
questions.explanation: Verses 10-11 describe the false prophets saying 'Peace' where there is none and building walls patched poorly with untempered mortar that will collapse under judgment.

questions.question: What does God promise to do to the wall patched with untempered mortar in Ezekiel 13:14?
options: Break it down to the foundation so it falls, consuming those who built it
Strengthen it to protect Israel forever
Cover it with gold as a sign of blessing
Ignore it and let it stand
questions.correctAnswer: Break it down to the foundation so it falls, consuming those who built it
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:14 reveals God's judgment by breaking down the faulty wall to its foundation, leading to the destruction of those who built it.

questions.question: What spiritual deception is described in Ezekiel 13:18 regarding the actions of certain women prophets?
options: They sew pillows on armholes and make kerchiefs to hunt souls
They lead people in idolatrous worship
They teach the law correctly
They serve as faithful intercessors
questions.correctAnswer: They sew pillows on armholes and make kerchiefs to hunt souls
questions.explanation: Verse 18 metaphorically accuses women prophets of crafting deceptive charms ('pillows' and 'kerchiefs') to ensnare souls, highlighting their false practices.

questions.question: What is the motive behind the women’s false prophecies as stated in Ezekiel 13:19?
options: They pollute God’s people for a few handfuls of barley and pieces of bread
They seek to bring true peace and repentance
They desire to encourage the righteous
They want to build the temple
questions.correctAnswer: They pollute God’s people for a few handfuls of barley and pieces of bread
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 13:19 reveals the women falsely prophesy for material gain, corrupting God’s people by promising life where there should be death.

questions.question: What does God declare He will do to the pillows and kerchiefs used by the women in Ezekiel 13:20-21?
options: Tear them from their arms and deliver His people from their hands
Bless them as tools of healing
Use them to protect His people
Hide them as sacred objects
questions.correctAnswer: Tear them from their arms and deliver His people from their hands
questions.explanation: Verses 20-21 show God's judgment in removing these deceptive items and rescuing His people from their spiritual manipulation.

questions.question: Which combined doctrinal truth emerges from Ezekiel 13:22 and 13:23 about the effects of false prophecy?
options: False prophecy saddens the righteous and strengthens the wicked by false promises of life
False prophecy leads to immediate repentance and forgiveness
False prophecy has no effect on the people of God
False prophecy only affects the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: False prophecy saddens the righteous and strengthens the wicked by false promises of life
questions.explanation: These verses teach that lies cause grief to the righteous and embolden the wicked by promising life falsely, but God will ultimately deliver His people.

questions.question: Theologically, what does Ezekiel 13:4's comparison of Israel's prophets to 'foxes in the deserts' symbolize?
options: The prophets are destructive and deceitful, undermining Israel's security
The prophets are swift messengers of God
The prophets provide shelter for the people
The prophets are wise and prudent
questions.correctAnswer: The prophets are destructive and deceitful, undermining Israel's security
questions.explanation: Verse 4 uses 'foxes' to depict prophets as cunning and harmful creatures that damage Israel’s spiritual defenses, reflecting their corrupt nature.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 13:16 contribute to the broader redemptive narrative regarding false peace?
options: It exposes false prophets claiming peace for Jerusalem when there is none, emphasizing God's true justice
It promises immediate restoration for Jerusalem
It describes the Messiah's reign of peace
It calls for Israel's conquest of neighboring nations
questions.correctAnswer: It exposes false prophets claiming peace for Jerusalem when there is none, emphasizing God's true justice
questions.explanation: Verse 16 warns against deceptive peace, highlighting God’s righteous judgment and the need for true restoration in redemptive history.

questions.question: What combined insight about God's protective justice is found in Ezekiel 13:9 and 13:15?
options: God excludes false prophets from His people and accomplishes His wrath on their false protections
God rewards false prophets for their efforts
God ignores the false prophets and their work
God blesses the wall they build
questions.correctAnswer: God excludes false prophets from His people and accomplishes His wrath on their false protections
questions.explanation: Verse 9 shows exclusion of false prophets from God's assembly, while verse 15 depicts God’s wrath destroying their false walls, demonstrating His justice.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God is indifferent to false prophecy and deception among His people. What does Ezekiel 13:8-9 actually teach about God's response?
options: God is actively against false prophets, bringing judgment and excluding them from His people
God tolerates false prophets for a time without consequence
God encourages false prophecy to test the people
God ignores the false prophets completely
questions.correctAnswer: God is actively against false prophets, bringing judgment and excluding them from His people
questions.explanation: Verses 8-9 clearly show God's opposition and judgment against false prophets, disproving claims of divine indifference.
